description:
## Dev build

This is a prerelease, not a regular release. It is not served as "latest", and the regular build stays on v1.33.0. The dev build contains YouTube and YouTube Music. Installing a dev module replaces the regular module of the same app, and the next regular build is then offered as an update.

## Features

### YouTube
- **Sync with anddea/revanced-patches dev:** The changes up to v4.4.0-dev.6 are merged into this fork.
- **Glass navigation bar spacing:** A bottom spacing slider in the Glass navigation bar size dialog sets how far the capsule floats above the bottom of the screen, and snackbars show right above the navigation bar.
- **Navigation bar fixes:** The buttons no longer sit too high with a black strip below them with the Translucent or Transparent style and gesture navigation, also when Glass navigation bar is off. The blurred background of the Translucent bar and of Glass is drawn only on Android 14 and newer; on Android 12 and 13 the bar keeps a plain translucent color, because the blur could crash the app while the player moves.
- **Feed cards:** With some accounts the cards had black gutters on both sides of the thumbnails, square corners, a small look, and an inline preview broke the cards around it. The margins and corners now follow the screen density, also after it changes, and grid cards such as the channel pages are clipped in their own columns. The dynamic colors tint the whole card below the thumbnail on these accounts too. Playlists, mixes and podcasts of the feed and the channel home follow the Classic layout or the card background like videos, and the cards keep their layout while the app updates its templates.
- **Unlock queue:** With Unlock queue on, "Play next in queue" in the feed menu uses YouTube's own queue. "Add to RVX queue" still opens the RVX queue dialog. Turn Unlock queue off to override the feed queue button. Premium-style queue takes priority when you turn it on.
- **About screen:** The About card moved into an About screen at the end of RVX settings.
- **Download option icons:** A new setting "Show download option icons", off by default, shows the icons beside Include subtitles and Include SponsorBlock in the built-in downloader when you turn it on.
- **Feature flags manager:** RVX settings > Miscellaneous > Debugging has a Feature flags manager, with Binary search to find which YouTube feature flag causes a problem. If the app fails to start twice in a row while flag overrides or a binary search are active, the third start resets them and tells you so.
- **Toolbar:** The Create button of the toolbar opens the upload menu again.
- **Watch later improvements:** New options to widen the drag handles of the Watch later videos and to hide the snackbar shown after removing a video.
- **Post buttons:** A Post buttons screen hides the like, share and comment buttons of posts, with an option to give every post the same grouped layout of buttons.
- **Captions:** Captions show in stable blocks and as two languages at once, on YouTube 21.15 and newer.
- **Spoof video streams:** The streams of a video are fetched sooner so videos start faster, and inline previews in the feed stay muted.

### YouTube Music
- **Lyrics:** A dynamic background for the lyrics, and the reading of each Japanese word above the text (furigana).
- **Play downloads locally:** Downloaded songs play from a private copy of their audio kept inside the app (about 5 MB a song). Radio, lyrics and the queue stay online while there is a connection; only the audio comes from the file. With no connection the copies play on their own, also with Spoof video streams on (the app keeps its own streams when there is no internet). The setting is off by default and independent of Download in app: on its own it saves only the copy, with Download in app also on, one download feeds both the files and the copy. A "Stream downloads" action shows what the copies take and deletes them all without touching saved files.
- **Green checks:** A green check at the right end of a song row (next to the menu or drag handle) means a stream copy exists. It shows on playlist pages, on the track rows of an album, in the Search songs filter and in the player queue, and on a playlist or album Download button when every available track has a copy. Songs saved only as files by Download in app are not marked: the check and local-file downloads are kept separate. The checks are on by default as a sub-setting of Play downloads locally.
- **Audio first:** A downloaded song starts in Song mode by default (a sub-setting, on by default), also from an album's track list, its Play button and Next. For a song without a saved video, the Song/Video switch still reaches the online video and keeps the playback position in both directions (the song starts over only when the position is unknown or within 3 seconds of the end).
- **Video copy:** Downloading an album also saves the 360p video of each song that has a music video, with the video's own audio (about 10 to 12 MB a video). Each song is matched to the video with the same title or about the same length, and a song with no certain match saves none. A playlist whose songs the server does not link to a music video saves audio only, and a song downloaded on its own gets no video. A video that cannot be saved never fails the song or the list. The finished message and the "Stream downloads" action count the videos and their size, tapping Download on a saved list fetches the videos it is missing, and deleting the stream downloads deletes the videos too.
- **Song and Video mode from the saved video:** A song with a saved video plays that saved video in both Song and Video mode, online and offline. The Song/Video switch is the app's own switch: it flips in place at once, with no reload, no stop of the sound and no change of position. Song mode plays the sound of the video itself. Tapping any song of an album, a playlist or the Downloads view starts that song this way, and Next and the end of a song go on in the mode you chose. Songs without a saved video keep their audio copy. Seeking works in Video mode offline too.
- **Offline cover and offline video:** With no connection, Song mode shows the song's album cover. For the saved videos to play offline, play one saved video online once after installing this version; the app then keeps the player settings the videos need.
- **Offline album taps:** With no connection, tapping a track of an album plays that track, not the first track of the album.
- **Offline replay:** Each copy keeps the details of its song, so it plays offline with its title and cover. Copies made before this version fill in these details by themselves while you are online. "Open downloaded songs" shows how many are offline ready.
- **No connection sheet:** The offline "No connection" sheet no longer covers the player controls while a downloaded song plays.
- **Playlists with unavailable tracks:** Deleted, private or blocked tracks (shown greyed out) no longer fail the whole download. The available tracks are downloaded and the finished message says how many were skipped ("N unavailable skipped"). A failed download names the reason in one line.
- **Downloads inside the Library:** Downloads is a chip view inside the Library page, with Songs, Playlists and Albums sub-chips that filter it. It works online and offline. The Library tab keeps the app's own behaviour and opens where you left it.
- **Offline playlist and album pages:** Opening a downloaded playlist or album online records the app's own page of it (about 90 KB per playlist, about 22 KB per album). Offline that page opens as it does online, with its header, cover, all rows and the checks, also when the album is opened from the Albums chip. Tapping a track plays its copy and the list continues from there.
- **Online or offline at the tap:** A Downloads row decides online or offline when you tap it, not when the page is drawn. This fixes a stale "Re-download?" dialog and a spinner when the network changed just before the tap.
- **Android Auto:** Stream copies are listed in a "Stream copies" folder inside Downloaded playlists, with their covers, and Android Auto downloaded playlists no longer needs Download in app. Android Auto keeps playing the audio copies.

## Compatibility
- YouTube: **21.39.525, 21.13.164, 20.05.46**.
- YouTube Music: **9.40.51, 9.15.51, 8.30.54**.

Not verified: the navigation bar fix on Android 15 and newer (no test device); the end of the Binary search of the Feature flags manager (unit-tested only); the light theme (the app's theme switch does not take effect on the test phone); YouTube 21.13.164 and 20.05.46 and YouTube Music 9.15.51 and 8.30.54 at runtime (the patches apply, but they were not run on a device); YouTube offline library serving after the Spoof video streams change; the reporter's feed card layout on an affected account (not reproducible on the test account, so the fix follows Morphe's); Android Auto (no head unit); playlists whose songs the server links to music videos (none were tested); auto-advance at the end of a song in Video mode; Previous in Video mode offline; a restored player offline (the stock restored player cannot play offline).

Known behaviour:
- A playlist or album page is recorded only when it is opened online. Until then, offline, it plays from its first downloaded song.
- Covers that were never seen online show as grey squares offline (only the app's image cache is used).
- A Downloads view built online and tapped right after the network drops can show a blank spinner for about 6 seconds before the page appears.
- With the setting "Device files" (IN_APP_DOWNLOADS) on, the Downloads view inside the Library is not reachable.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/lavinhoque33/revanced-patches/compare/v1.34.0-dev.3...v1.34.0-dev.4)
